Midcap150 Momentum 10 — Report 48, Rebalance Month Offset

Report 48's exact design — the 200-day EMA regime filter, gold instead of cash — tested across all 6 semi-annual rebalance calendars: June/December (report 48's own convention), July/January, August/February, September/March, October/April, and November/May. Report 25 already tested this exact idea on the plain (no-filter) strategy; this asks whether the calendar offset matters once the gold-hedged regime filter is layered on top. Same continuous daily 200-EMA regime check throughout — only the stock-selection calendar changes between the 6 variants.

2009-02-27–2026-08-24
Report generated 2026-09-29 23:42
▲ report 48's own June/December calendar is the SAFEST of all six, but not the highest-CAGR one

Among all 6 gold-hedged variants, June/December still has the SHALLOWEST drawdown (-23.4%) — but it's no longer the lowest CAGR once November/May is added to the comparison: November / May now has the lowest CAGR (+41.4%) of the six, and its drawdown isn't particularly good either (-25.3%) — it doesn't win on either axis. The best CAGR still belongs to July / January (+44.7%), at the cost of the deepest drawdown of the six (-26.0%).

The spread here is real but not huge — CAGR ranges about 3 percentage points across all 6 calendars, and drawdown ranges about 2.6 points. This is a genuinely different, smaller-magnitude question than report 25's finding on the plain strategy, since the 200-EMA regime filter (identical daily signal in all 6 variants) is doing most of the risk-reduction work regardless of which two months the stock picks happen to refresh in.

Why the offset matters less here than it did for the plain strategy

▲ framing

WHAT THIS SHOWS — the mechanism, not just the scoreboard.

Report 25 found the rebalance calendar mattered for the PLAIN momentum strategy because with no regime filter, the stock-selection calendar is the ONLY lever determining when the portfolio reacts to changing conditions. Here, the 200-EMA regime filter reacts to NIFTY 50's close EVERY SINGLE DAY, completely independent of which two months the stock picks happen to refresh in — the calendar only controls which specific 10 stocks are held DURING an "on" stretch, not whether the strategy is exposed to the market at all. That's a smaller lever, which is why the spread here (about 2 points of CAGR, 2.6 of drawdown) is real but modest.

Report 48's June/December choice was inherited from this project's original momentum-formula convention (NSE's own semi-annual reconstitution cadence), not chosen for its risk/return profile specifically. This report shows that choice happens to land on the safest end of the offset spectrum, not the highest-return end — a reasonable trade to have made, even if not deliberately optimized for.

Limitations

▲ read before trusting any number above

WHAT THIS SHOWS — every simplification behind this backtest.

  • All six possible semi-annual offsets are now covered — this is the complete set, not a sample of it — but each is still only ONE specific two-month pairing, not a sweep of every possible single-month rebalance date.
  • The common comparison window starts a little later than report 48's own (2009-02-27 vs. report 48's 2009-01-02) because six different calendars each take a slightly different number of days to first reach a valid 252-day-lookback rebalance — the intersection of all six pushes the shared start date out.
  • Zero transaction costs on any regime switch or scheduled rebalance — same disclosed omission as every other reconstruction here.
  • Today's fixed Midcap150 constituent list is applied retroactively across the whole window (survivorship bias). Equal weighting, no F&O-eligibility screen, unadjusted prices, no dividends modeled — same as every other reconstruction here.
